topics.label: Introduction and course overview
topics.groupedBecause: It introduces the lecture series, outlines the learning objectives, and frames cancer biology for the interdisciplinary student audience.

topics.label: Cellular differentiation, genetic alterations, and tumor modeling
topics.groupedBecause: They explain how cancer originates from accumulated genetic alterations and disrupted tissue differentiation programs, along with the laboratory methods used to study them.

topics.label: Tumor invasion, metastasis, and the colorectal progression model
topics.groupedBecause: They examine the mechanisms and histological features of local invasion and metastasis, illustrated by the stepwise adenoma-to-carcinoma sequence in colorectal cancer.

topics.label: Classification and nomenclature of benign and malignant tumors
topics.groupedBecause: They outline the clinical behavior, physical risks, and systematic naming conventions used to categorize benign and malignant neoplasms.

topics.label: Pathophysiological causes of cancer morbidity and mortality
topics.groupedBecause: It explains the physiological mechanisms by which primary and metastatic tumors cause organ dysfunction, systemic complications, and death.

topics.label: Comparative cancer incidence across humans and animal taxa
topics.groupedBecause: They analyze the epidemiological incidence and mortality of cancers in human populations and across diverse animal species.

topics.label: Clinical detection and cancer screening strategies
topics.groupedBecause: They evaluate the clinical rationale, procedures, and varying effectiveness of screening programs for detecting early and pre-malignant tumors.

topics.label: Conclusion and session closing
topics.groupedBecause: It concludes the lecture with a reminder of the learning outcomes and housekeeping for upcoming practicals and lectures.
